overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts data reveals a strong viewer preference for extreme planetary science and cosmic 'What If' scenarios. Videos featuring immersive hypothetical explorations of bizarre celestial bodies (e.g., liquid diamond planets, planets of burning ice, dark planets) generate the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view) compared to standard psychology or animal facts, which underperformed.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) outperform standard trivia formats by large margins.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/exploration scenarios involving extreme physics and exotic materials.

winning_patterns.evidence: Content highlighting bizarre planetary physics, such as TrES-2b ('The Planet Darker Than Coal', 1,030 views) and Venus's unusual rotation (981 views), drives high sustained viewership.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing lesser-known exoplanets with extreme, counter-intuitive environmental conditions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts focusing on brain tricks and memory facts (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') consistently underperformed, hovering between 5 and 53 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychology micro-facts unless framed as a high-stakes neurological mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (when published outside recent surges) or basic lifespans showed low overall traction compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than simple trivia.

fresh_topic_constraints: Do not mention diamond planets, burning ice, or TrES-2b
Must feature an entirely new exoplanet/space phenomenon not found in the historical dataset
Keep pacing under 15 seconds to maximize loop retention

experiment: Test a 15-second space 'What If' scenario against a 20-second cinematic animal survival micro-story to see if audience retention scales better with cosmic dread or biological tension.
